title: Crystallised flower petals
subtitle: fresh edible flower petals coated in egg white and caster sugar and dried until crisp
excerpt: Crystallised flower petals are made by brushing fresh edible petals with beaten egg white, dusting them in caster sugar, and leaving them to dry on a rack until the coating is firm and translucent. The finished petals last several weeks in an airtight container and are used to decorate cakes, tarts, and desserts.
sourceNotes: Crystallised flowers were widely used in British and French confectionery from the seventeenth century onward. Violets, roses, and borage were among the most commonly preserved. Traditional recipes appear in Mrs Beeton and in French confiserie manuals.

content.text: Crystallised flower petals are fresh edible petals coated in egg white and caster sugar, then dried until the coating is crisp and translucent. Violets, rose petals, pansies, borage, and lavender all crystallise well. The dried petals keep their colour and shape for several weeks in a sealed container at room temperature.
Use only flowers that are known to be edible. Some garden flowers are toxic. If in doubt about a variety, do not use it.
Pick the flowers in the morning once the dew has dried but before the heat of the day wilts them. Use the same day.
Beat one egg white lightly with a fork until just broken up and pourable but not foamy. For large batches, use pasteurised liquid egg white.
Hold a petal or small flower by its stem or base. Paint a thin, even layer of egg white over every surface, including the back. Avoid clumps or pools of egg white.
Dust or sift caster sugar over both sides of the coated petal immediately. The sugar should stick in an even layer. Shake off any excess over a sheet of baking paper.

Place on a cooling rack lined with baking paper. Leave at room temperature in a warm, dry place for 24 to 48 hours until the coating is firm and crisp to the touch. If the room is humid, dry in an oven on the lowest setting (50 degrees C) with the door ajar for 2 to 3 hours.
Store in a single layer in an airtight container between sheets of baking paper. Keeps for up to 4 weeks at room temperature.

attrs.problem: Petals wilting and losing shape during drying
attrs.avoid: Avoid thick or wet egg white; it weighs the petals down and the sugar coating becomes too heavy to hold the shape.
attrs.fix: Use a thin wash of egg white and shake off all excess before sugaring. Very delicate petals (violet, borage) may need propping with a small fold of paper while they dry.

attrs.problem: Sugar coating falling off after drying
attrs.avoid: Avoid too little egg white; the sugar has nothing to stick to.
attrs.fix: The egg white layer must cover every surface including the back. If sugar still falls off, apply a second thin coat of egg white over the dried first coat and re-sugar.
